types.name: FDebugLineStyle
types.doc:
How a thick primitive is drawn. Thickness and halo are in output pixels, so
a line reads the same at one metre and at a kilometre.

members.name: Halo
members.doc:
Dark outline on each side of the core. What keeps a saturated colour
legible over a background of the same brightness: the gizmo's green
over sunlit grass, its blue over a night sky.

members.name: Lifetime
members.doc:
Seconds. 0 draws this frame only; a negative value keeps the primitive
until ClearPersistent.

members.name: DrawThickLine
members.signature: void DrawThickLine(const Vec3& a, const Vec3& b, const Vec4& color, const FDebugLineStyle& style)
members.doc:
The line batcher. DrawLine above stays the cheap one-pixel path for bulk
debug geometry (a navmesh is hundreds of thousands of edges); these are
the anti-aliased, screen-space-thick primitives the editor's own overlays
draw with, batched into one stream per depth priority and drawn after
the selection outline.

types.name: ETransformGizmoHandle
types.doc: Same order and values as the editor's EGizmoAxis, so the two convert by value.

members.name: Scale
members.doc:
World length of one axis — the caller keeps it a constant fraction of
the viewport height, which is what makes the gizmo screen-sized.

types.name: FTransformGizmoMetrics
types.doc:
The gizmo's geometry and widths. A plain header struct rather than members
of the exported class below: a static data member of a dllimport class is
not a constant expression to MSVC, and the editor's hit test initialises
its own constants from these.

members.name: kAxisLength
members.doc:
Geometry as fractions of Scale. FGizmoSystem's hit test reads the same
numbers, so what is drawn is what can be grabbed.

members.name: kScreenFraction
members.doc: Axis length as a fraction of the viewport height.

types.name: FTransformGizmoDraw
types.doc:
The transform gizmo's look, kept out of the editor so a test can draw the
exact gizmo the editor draws and measure it on screen. Everything goes
through the Foreground batch: unlit display-referred colour after the
tonemapper, a constant pixel width with an anti-aliased edge, a dark halo,
and dithering where scene geometry stands in front of a handle.
